content: 1. Participation in this survey is entirely voluntary. You have the right to withdraw from the survey at any time without facing any penalties or consequences. 2. You may choose not to participate in any part of the survey that makes you uncomfortable. 3. You are not obligated to answer any questions that you do not wish to respond to. 4. If you decide to withdraw from the survey, it will not affect your access to healthcare services or medications in any way. 5. If you have any questions or concerns about the study or your participation, you can contact the principal investigator or the institution conducting the study. 6. If you have questions or concerns about the ethical aspects of the study, you can contact a representative from the ethics committee or the institution overseeing the project. 7. If you agree to participate in the survey, please print your name and sign the consent form. 8. Signing the consent form does not mean you are giving up any of your legal rights. 9. You will be provided with a copy of the signed consent form for your records. 10. The survey is sponsored by [insert sponsor name]. Introduction 11. My name is [insert name], and I work for [insert organization]. We are conducting this study to understand the prevalence of certain diseases, specifically hepatitis B and hepatitis C, among people in [Country X]. 12. This study involves taking a blood sample to determine if you have hepatitis. 13. No monetary compensation will be provided for your participation. 14. We have already informed your parent(s) or guardian(s) about this study, and they are aware that we are asking for your participation. 15. Before deciding, you are encouraged to seek advice from anyone you trust. 16. You can take your time to decide whether or not to participate, and you can change your mind at any point. Purpose 17. You were randomly selected to participate in this study on hepatitis. 18. Hepatitis is a disease that affects the liver. 19. There is an effective vaccine available to prevent hepatitis B, but there is no vaccine for hepatitis C. However, hepatitis C can be treated and cured with effective medications. 20. The purpose of this study is to determine how many people are affected by hepatitis B and C. 21. The results of this survey will help us improve prevention and treatment strategies for these diseases. What Will Happen 22. The study will take approximately 15 minutes. 23. First, we will ask you some questions about your vaccination history. 24. Then, we will collect a small blood sample by drawing blood from a vein. The amount of blood taken will be specified based on the tests being performed. 25. The blood sample will be tested in a laboratory for hepatitis B and C. Risks, Discomforts, and Benefits 26. The process of drawing blood may cause mild pain, similar to a mosquito bite. 27. There may be minor bleeding, bruising, or swelling at the site where the blood is drawn. 28. If the blood test shows that you have hepatitis B or C, healthcare professionals will inform you and provide guidance on treatment options. 29. Your test results will remain confidential and will only be shared with you and your parent(s) or guardian(s). Contact Information 30. If you have any questions, you can contact Dr. [insert name] at [insert phone number]. 31. For test results, you can call [insert phone number]. 32. Your unique participant number is [insert number]. Certificate of Assent 33. I understand that this research is about hepatitis, that I will answer some questions and provide a blood sample, and that I will be informed and offered care if I test positive for hepatitis. 34. I have read this information (or had it read to me), and I have had my questions answered. I understand that I can ask additional questions at any time. 35. I agree to participate in this research. 36. [Child’s initials, printed name, signature, and date to be filled in if the child assents.] 37. If the child is illiterate, a literate witness (not a parent or someone connected to the research team) must sign and confirm that the child has freely given consent. Recommendations for Preand Post-Test Counseling 38. Testing for viral hepatitis must follow the principles of the 5 Cs: Consent: Testing must be voluntary, with informed consent obtained. Participants should be informed about the testing process and their right to decline. Confidentiality: All discussions and test results must remain confidential. Personal information, including test results, should not be disclosed without the participant’s consent. Counseling: Pre-test information and post-test counseling must be provided to ensure participants understand their results and next steps. Correct: Testing services must ensure accurate diagnoses through quality assurance mechanisms. Positive results should be confirmed with additional testing before initiating treatment. Connection: Participants should be linked to appropriate prevention, treatment, and care services, with effective follow-up and long-term support.
